latin.2671: THESIS I. In eo statu homo a Deo conditus est ut posset legi quam Deus ipsi tulit obedientiam integram & perfectam praestare absque omni labe vel culpa. Nec enim aequum fuisset Deum ab innocenti creatura ea exigere ad quae praestanda, vel nullas, vel non sufficientes vires ei concessisset. Atque hoc confirmat scriptura, dum docet [marg.: Eccl. 7. 29.] Deum fecisse hominem rectum. Nec enim posset censeri rectus ille qui sese legi Dei, quae rectitudinis norma est, conformare non posset.
latin.2672: II. Verum homo sponte legem Dei transgressus, amisit ea dona & auxilia per quae poterat legem Dei servare; & ita peccati servus effectus est, ut ex se, nequidem in uno opere, omni ex parte legi satisfacere possit, Deoque gratum & acceptum obsequium exhibere: tantum abest ut legem sic adimplere queat, ut necesse est ei qui per legem vult ad vitam pervenire. Quod Scriptura sacra satis aperte docet, dum affirmat [marg.: Eph. 2.] homines, extra Christi gratiam, in peccatis esse mortuos, & [marg.: Joan. 15.] nos sine illo nihil posse facere: neque [marg.: 2 Cor. 3.] sufficientes esse cogitare aliquid a nobis, quasi ex nobis: ac [marg.: Rom. 8.] sapientiam carnis inimicam esse Deo, & legi Dei subjectam non esse, neque se subjicere posse.
latin.2673: III. Sed Deus generis humani, culpa sua perditi, misertus, in mundum misit Christum filium suum, qui non solum homines liberaret a poenis, quas peccatis suis juste commeriti erant: Verum etiam illos a servitute peccati eximeret, & eam conferret gratiam, per quam rursus possent Deo in vera justitia & sanctitate servire, novamque mandatis ejus inchoare obedientiam.
latin.2674: IV. Hanc gratiam, tanquam pertinentem ad novum foedus in Christo ineundum, Deus per Prophetas saepius promisit. Sic enim loquitur Deus apud Ezechielem, cap. 11. Dabo eis cor unum, & spiritum novum tribuam in visceribus eorum: & auferam cor lapideum de carne eorum, & dabo eis cor carneum: ut in praeceptis meis ambulent, & judicia mea custodiant, faciantque ea: & sint mihi in populum, & ego sim eis in Deum. Et rursus cap. 36. Effundam super vos aquam mundam, & mundabimini ab omnibus inquinamentis vestris, & ab universis idolis vestris mundabo vos. Et dabo vobis cor novum, & spiritum novum ponam in medio vestri: & auferam cor lapideum de carne vestra, & dabo vobis cor carneum. Et spiritum meum ponam in medio vestri: & faciam ut in praeceptis meis ambuletis, & judicia mea custodiatis & operemini. Et habitabitis in terra quam dedi Patribus vestris: & eritis mihi in populum, & ego ero vobis in Deum.
latin.2675: V. Quibus consona sunt quae habentur apud Jeremiam, cap. 31. Ecce dies venient, dicit Dominus, & feriam domui Israel, & domui Juda, foedus novum. Non secundum pactum quod pepigi cum patribus vestris in die qua apprehendi manum eorum, ut educerem eos de terra Aegypti: quod pactum irritum fecerunt, & ego dominatus sum eorum, dicit Dominus. Sed hoc erit pactum quod feriam cum domo Israel post dies illos, dicit Dominus. Dabo legem meam in visceribus eorum, & in corde eorum scribam eam: & ero eis in Deum, & ipsi erunt mihi in populum. Et cap. sequenti, Dabo eis cor unum & viam unam, ut timeant me universis diebus: & bene sit eis, & filiis eorum post eos. Et feriam eis pactum sempiternum: & non desinam eis benefacere: & timorem meum dabo in corde eorum: ut non recedant a me.
latin.2676: VI. Similia quoque praedixerat Moses, Deut. 30. Circumcidet, inquit, Dominus Deus tuus cor tuum, & cor seminis tui, ut diligas Dominum Deum tuum ex toto corde tuo, & in tota anima tua, ut possis vivere. Et paulo post, Tu autem reverteris, & audies vocem Domini Dei tui, faciesque universa mandata quae ego praecipio tibi hodie. Et abundare te faciet Dominus Deus tuus in cunctis operibus manuum tuarum.
latin.2677: VII. Et certe, nisi Deus talem hominibus gratiam largiretur per quam possent verum & sincerum divinis mandatis obsequium praebere, nullus eorum salvus esse posset, & legitime confidere Deum erga ipsum usurum beneficentia & misericordia illa, quam nobis in Christo offert & exhibet. Nec enim Deus cum aliis misericorditer & benigne acturum sese pollicetur, quam cum iis qui foedus ejus servant, & mandata illius faciunt. Ut videre est, Psal. 103. Misericordia autem Domini ab aeterno & usque in aeternum super timentes eum: & justitia ejus in filios filiorum. His qui servant testamentum ejus, & memores sunt mandatorum ipsius ad faciendum ea. Quibus congruit illud quod legitur apud Ezechielem, cap. 18. Si autem impius egerit poenitentiam ab omnibus peccatis suis quae operatus est, & custodierit omnia praecepta mea, & fecerit judicium & justitiam: vita vivet & non morietur. Omnium iniquitatum ejus, quas operatus est non recordabor: in justitia sua quam operatus est vivet.
latin.2678: VIII. Eodem etiam spectat quod Christus in Apocalypsi beatos demum pronunciat illos qui mandata Dei custodiunt. Omnes autem eos qui vitiis indulgent, quique amant & faciunt mendacium, a civitate Dei excludendos declarat. Beati, inquit, qui custodiunt mandata illius, ut sit potestas eorum in ligno vitae, & per portas intrent in civitatem. Foris autem canes, & venefici, & impudici, & homicidae, & idolis servientes, & omnis qui amat & facit mendacium, Apoc. 22.
latin.2679: IX. Neque vero quisquam est in communione Christi, aut eum vere nosse & amare censeri potest, qui mandata Dei non servet. In hoc scimus, inquit Johannes, quoniam cognovimus eum, si mandata ejus observamus. Qui dicit se nosse Deum, & mandata ejus non custodit, mendax est, & veritas in eo non est. 1 Joan. 2. & cap. 3. Qui servat mandata ejus in illo manet, & ipse in eo. Similiter cap. 5. Haec est charitas Dei ut mandata ejus custodiamus. Unde est quod Paulus, 1 Cor. 7. solam observationem mandatorum Dei alicujus momenti in Christo esse docet, Circumcisio, inquit, nihil est: & praeputium nihil est: sed observatio mandatorum Dei.
latin.2680: X. Verum fideles per divinam gratiam posse Dei mandata servare omnium evidentissime probat ipsa experientia. Nam, Scriptura teste, multi sancti & pii homines de facto Dei mandata servarunt. Id de seipso David affirmare non veretur, Psal. 119. [marg.: Pausa Heth.] Festinavi, inquit, & non tardavi custodire mandata tua. Item, [marg.: Pausa Schin.] Custodivit anima mea testimonia tua: & dilexit ea vehementer. Servavi mandata tua & testimonia tua: quia omnes viae meae in conspectu tuo. Lucas autem Evangelista idem testimonium perhibet de Zacharia & Elizabeth illius uxore. Erant, inquit, justi ambo ante Deum, incedentes in omnibus mandatis & justificationibus Domini, sine querela. Quin omnes pii & fideles in scriptura frequenter describuntur per eos qui mandata Dei custodiunt: Ut quum dicit David psalmo modo citato, Socius ego sum omnium timentium te, & custodientium mandata tua.
latin.2681: XI. Itaque jure merito Joannes epist. primae cap. quinto affirmat mandata Dei non esse gravia. Etenim, praeterquam quod nihil a nobis exigunt quod naturae & rationi valde consentaneum, & nobis maxime conducibile non sit, Deus etiam suis vires sufficit, per quas mandata ejus effecta dare possint, & per gratiam suam praestat, ut illa pii & fideles observent.
latin.2682: XII. Porro cum fideles, in quibus gratia divina operatur, dicantur in scriptura Dei mandata servare, dubium non est quin aliquo etiam sensu, dici possint Dei legem implere. Nam Dei mandata sunt idem cum Dei lege. Dei vero mandata servare, & illa eadem implere unum idemque significant. Et certe negari non potest quin vera & sincera charitas, id est, dilectio Dei & proximi, reperiatur in eis qui per spiritum Dei regeniti sunt. Nam qui credunt in Christum, & sunt per spiritum ejus denuo nati, transiverunt a morte ad vitam. Sed, ut testatur Joannes Apostolus, Qui non diligit manet in morte. 1 Joan. 3. Ac perinde quicunque spirituali vita vivunt, necessario Deum & proximum diligunt. Charitas autem est impletio legis, & qui diligit, legem implevit, ut expresse docet Paulus, Rom. 13.
latin.2683: XIII. Praeterea justitiam legis in nobis impleri, & nos legem & ejus justitiam implere eodem plane recidere videntur. Jam vero docet Apostolus Christum in hunc mundum venisse ut justitia legis impleretur in nobis, qui non ambulamus secundum carnem, sed secundum spiritum. Nam, inquit, quod erat impossibile legi, quia per carnem infirma erat, Deus filium suum mittens, in similitudinem carnis peccati, & de peccato, damnavit peccatum in carne, ut justificatio, sive justitia legis impleretur in nobis, qui non ambulamus secundum carnem, sed secundum spiritum. Rom. 8.
latin.2684: XIV. Porro, quamvis vero & commodo sensu dici possint qui spiritu Dei aguntur Dei legem implere, & ejus mandata servare, juxta Scripturae stylum & consuetudinem: multum tamen ab eo absunt, ut possint legem perfecte implere, & Dei praeceptis exactam atque omnibus numeris absolutam obedientiam praebere.
latin.2685: XV. Nam perfecte legem implere est omni ex parte legi satisfacere, secundum totum illius rigorem, nec deficere in ullo eorum, quae lex praecise sumpta ab homine postulat, ut possit vi foederis legalis, juxta Clausulam Fac & vives, ad vitam pervenire, & foelicitatem quam lex pollicetur pro jure suo exigere, absque ullo metu poenarum quas lex comminatur praevaricatoribus. Nemo autem eo sensu & respectu legem implet, nisi qui prorsus immunis est a peccato, nec unquam legem transgressus est. Omnes enim qui vel semel peccaverunt, lex rigide sumpta judicat & damnat, & addicit maledictioni, juxta alteram istam terribilem Clausulam, Maledictus omnis qui non permanserit in omnibus quae scripta sunt in libro legis hujus ad faciendum ea. Quippe lex neminem gratis justificat & absolvit, sed tantum ex debito, secundum Pauli doctrinam, Rom. 4. Omnis peccator autem, quicunque tandem ille sit, eget Dei gratia & misericordia, nec nisi gratis justificari potest.
latin.2686: XVI. Jam vero nullus est hominum qui legem non sit quandoque transgressus. Si quidem omnes in peccato nascuntur, & per naturam servi sunt peccati, imo in peccatis mortui, atque in ea morte & servitute perpetuo jacerent, nisi inde per Christi gratiam excitarentur & liberarentur. Quod jam breviter supra ostendimus: idemque Scriptura toties & tam aperte inculcat, ut superfluum videatur testimonia ejus hac de re congerere. Praesertim vero Paulus hanc doctrinam saepius urget atque ingerit in suis Epistolis, & maxime in ea quam scripsit ad Romanos quatuor primis capitibus. Ubi pluribus argumentis convincit, Omnes peccavisse & Omnes, tam Judaeos quam Graecos, esse sub peccato, juxta illa Scripturae dicta, Non est justus quisquam, non est intelligens, non est requirens Deum. Omnes declinaverunt, simul inutiles facti sunt; non est qui faciat bonum, non est usque ad unum. Unde concludit neminem ex operibus legis coram Deo justificari: sed omnes justificari gratis per gratiam Dei per redemptionem quae est in Christo Jesu. Ex eo vero sequitur nullum esse qui legem Dei perfecte & omni ex parte impleat: quandoquidem, si quis legem eo modo impleret, proculdubio per opera legis justificaretur, idque ex debito, non autem ex gratia.
latin.2687: XVII. Verum non solum homines sunt per naturam peccato immersi, & per legem peccati convicti: sed etiam postquam sunt per gratiam renati, multum ab eo absunt ut undiquaque perfectum obsequium legi praestent. Etenim sanctissimi quique in multa peccata quotidie labuntur: Juxta illud Jacobi, In multis offendimus omnes. [marg.: Jac. 3.] Et Joannis epistola prima cap. 1. Si dixerimus quod peccatum non habemus, ipsi nos seducimus, & veritas in nobis non est. Quibus congruit quod pronunciat sapiens, Eccl. cap. 7. Non est homo justus in terra qui faciat bonum, & non peccet.
latin.2688: XVIII. Neque tantum levioribus & minutis peccatis homines per Christi gratiam regeniti obnoxii manent: sed vix ulli eorum sunt qui non quandoque incidant in gravia peccata; quibus novo mortis aeternae reatu constricti tenentur, & praesentem aptitudinem ad regnum coeleste amittunt, donec speciali Dei gratia excitante, inde per singularem poenitentiam resurgant. Id manifestum faciunt frequentes sanctorum lapsus in Scriptura memorati, ut Davidis, qui incidit in adulterium & homicidium: & Petri, qui ter Christum cum juramento abnegavit. Idemque nimis saepe confirmat quotidiana fidelium experientia.

sections.title: Man was created able to obey the law perfectly
sections.pass_a: THESIS I. In that state man was made by God that he could render to the law which God gave him an entire & perfect obedience without any stain or fault. For it would not have been fair for God to demand from an innocent creature those things for performing which he had granted him either no powers, or not sufficient ones. And Scripture confirms this, when it teaches [margin: Eccl. 7:29] that God made man upright. For he could not be judged upright who could not conform himself to the law of God, which is the rule of uprightness.
pass_b: Thesis I. God created man in a condition in which he could give the law God laid on him a complete and perfect obedience, free of any stain or fault. It would not have been fair for God to require of an innocent creature what he had given it no strength, or not enough strength, to do.
Scripture confirms this when it teaches (margin: Eccl. 7:29) that God made man upright; and no one could count as upright who was unable to conform himself to God's law, the very rule of uprightness.

choices.why: The locus question: whether and how far a person can fulfil the law through Christ's grace.

sections.title: Fallen man cannot keep the law of himself
sections.pass_a: II. But man, having willingly transgressed the law of God, lost those gifts & helps through which he could keep the law of God; & so he was made the slave of sin, that of himself, not even in one work, can he satisfy the law in every respect, & show God a pleasing & acceptable obedience: so far is he from being able to fulfil the law in the way that is necessary for one who wants to reach life through the law. Which sacred Scripture teaches plainly enough, when it affirms [margin: Eph. 2] that men, outside the grace of Christ, are dead in sins, & [margin: John 15] that we without him can do nothing: and [margin: 2 Cor. 3] that we are not sufficient to think anything of ourselves, as of ourselves: and [margin: Rom. 8] that the wisdom of the flesh is hostile to God, & is not subject to the law of God, nor can subject itself.
pass_b: Thesis II. But man broke God's law of his own accord and lost the gifts and helps by which he had been able to keep it. He thus became the slave of sin, so that of himself he cannot satisfy the law fully in even a single work, or offer God an obedience that pleases him and that he accepts. Much less can he fulfil the law as anyone must who wants to reach life by the law.

Holy Scripture teaches this plainly enough. It says that people outside Christ's grace are dead in sins (margin: Eph. 2); that without him we can do nothing (margin: John 15); that we are not sufficient to think anything of ourselves, as if from ourselves (margin: 2 Cor. 3); and that the wisdom of the flesh is hostile to God, is not subject to God's law and cannot be (margin: Rom. 8).

lemmas.gloss: satisfy the law in every respect

choices.why: The locus question: whether and how far a person can fulfil the law through Christ's grace.

sections.title: Christ came to free us from sin's slavery as well as its penalty
sections.pass_a: III. But God, having pity on the human race, ruined by its own fault, sent into the world Christ his son, who should not only free men from the punishments, which they had justly deserved by their sins: But also deliver them from the slavery of sin, & confer that grace, through which they could again serve God in true righteousness & holiness, & begin a new obedience to his commandments.
pass_b: Thesis III. But God took pity on the human race, lost through its own fault, and sent his Son Christ into the world. Christ was not only to free people from the punishments their sins had justly earned, but also to release them from slavery to sin.
He was to give them the grace by which they could once more serve God in true righteousness and holiness and make a start on a new obedience to his commandments.

lemmas.gloss: deliver from the slavery of sin
begin a new obedience to his commandments

choices.why: The locus question: whether and how far a person can fulfil the law through Christ's grace.

sections.title: The grace of the new covenant promised in Ezekiel
sections.pass_a: IV. This grace, as belonging to the new covenant to be made in Christ, God promised quite often through the Prophets. For thus God speaks in Ezekiel, chap. 11. I will give them one heart, & I will put a new spirit within them: & I will take away the stony heart from their flesh, & I will give them a heart of flesh: that they may walk in my precepts, & keep my judgments, and do them: & that they may be my people, & I may be their God. And again chap. 36. I will pour clean water upon you, & you shall be cleansed from all your filthiness, & from all your idols I will cleanse you. And I will give you a new heart, & put a new spirit in the midst of you: & I will take away the stony heart from your flesh, & give you a heart of flesh. And I will put my spirit in the midst of you: & I will cause you to walk in my precepts, & to keep my judgments & do them. And you shall dwell in the land which I gave to your Fathers: & you shall be my people, & I will be your God.
pass_b: Thesis IV. God often promised this grace through the prophets, as belonging to the new covenant to be made in Christ. In Ezekiel 11 he says: 'I will give them one heart and put a new spirit within them. I will take the heart of stone out of their flesh and give them a heart of flesh, so that they walk in my precepts, keep my judgments and do them, and so that they are my people and I am their God.'

And again in chapter 36: 'I will pour clean water on you, and you will be made clean from all your defilements; from all your idols I will cleanse you. I will give you a new heart and put a new spirit within you. I will take the heart of stone out of your flesh and give you a heart of flesh. I will put my Spirit within you and make you walk in my precepts, keep my judgments and carry them out. You will live in the land I gave your fathers; you will be my people, and I will be your God.'

lemmas.latin: faciam ut in praeceptis meis ambuletis
lemmas.gloss: I will cause you to walk in my precepts

choices.why: The prophetic promise of the covenant of grace under which the law is written on the heart.

sections.title: The same promise in Jeremiah
sections.pass_a: V. In agreement with which are the things found in Jeremiah, chap. 31. Behold the days will come, says the Lord, & I will make with the house of Israel, & with the house of Judah, a new covenant. Not according to the covenant which I made with your fathers in the day when I took their hand, to bring them out of the land of Egypt: which covenant they made void, & I was lord over them, says the Lord. But this shall be the covenant which I will make with the house of Israel after those days, says the Lord. I will put my law in their inward parts, & in their heart I will write it: & I will be their God, & they shall be my people. And in the following chap., I will give them one heart & one way, that they may fear me all their days: & that it may be well with them, & with their children after them. And I will make with them an everlasting covenant: & I will not cease to do them good: & I will put my fear in their heart: that they may not depart from me.
pass_b: Thesis V. What we read in Jeremiah 31 agrees with this: 'The days are coming, says the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and the house of Judah. It will not be like the covenant I made with your fathers on the day I took them by the hand to lead them out of Egypt, a covenant they broke, and I was lord over them, says the Lord.

This is the covenant I will make with the house of Israel after those days, says the Lord: I will put my law within them and write it on their hearts; I will be their God, and they will be my people.' And in the next chapter: 'I will give them one heart and one way, so that they fear me all their days, and that it may be well with them and with their children after them. I will make an everlasting covenant with them and never stop doing them good, and I will put the fear of me in their hearts, so that they do not turn away from me.'

lemmas.latin: Dabo legem meam in visceribus eorum
lemmas.gloss: I will put my law in their inward parts
that they may not depart from me

choices.why: The prophetic promise of the covenant of grace under which the law is written on the heart.

sections.title: Moses foretold the same
sections.pass_a: VI. Moses also had foretold similar things, Deut. 30. The Lord your God, he says, will circumcise your heart, & the heart of your seed, that you may love the Lord your God with all your heart, & with all your soul, that you may live. And a little after, But you shall return, & hear the voice of the Lord your God, and do all the commandments which I command you today. And the Lord your God will make you abound in all the works of your hands.
pass_b: Thesis VI. Moses too had foretold something similar. In Deuteronomy 30 the promise runs: the Lord your God will circumcise your heart and your offspring's heart, so that you love him with all your heart and all your soul, so that you may live.

Shortly afterwards come the words: 'Then you will return, hearing the Lord your God's voice and carrying out every commandment I command you today; and the Lord your God will make you abound in all the works of your hands.'

choices.why: The prophetic promise of the covenant of grace under which the law is written on the heart.

sections.title: Without such grace no one could be saved
sections.pass_a: VII. And certainly, unless God bestowed on men such grace through which they could render a true & sincere obedience to the divine commandments, none of them could be saved, & rightly trust that God will use toward him that beneficence & mercy, which he offers & shows us in Christ. For God does not promise that he will deal mercifully & kindly with any others, than with those who keep his covenant, & do his commandments. As may be seen, Psal. 103. But the mercy of the Lord is from eternity & to eternity upon those who fear him: & his righteousness unto children's children. To those who keep his covenant, & are mindful of his commandments to do them. With which agrees what is read in Ezekiel, chap. 18. But if the wicked man shall do penance for all his sins which he has committed, & shall keep all my precepts, & shall do judgment & righteousness: living he shall live & shall not die. Of all his iniquities, which he has committed I will not remember: in his righteousness which he has wrought he shall live.
pass_b: Thesis VII. Certainly, if God did not give people a grace by which they could offer his commandments true and sincere obedience, none of them could be saved, or have good grounds for trusting that God will show him the kindness and mercy he offers and grants us in Christ. God promises to deal mercifully and kindly only with those who keep his covenant and carry out his commandments.

So Psalm 103: 'The Lord's mercy is from everlasting to everlasting on those who fear him, and his righteousness reaches their children's children, those who keep his covenant and remember his commandments so as to do them.' Ezekiel 18 agrees: 'If the wicked man repents of all the sins he has committed, keeps all my precepts and does what is just and right, he will surely live; he will not die. I will not remember any of the wrongs he has done; he will live by the righteousness he has practised.'

lemmas.gloss: a true and sincere obedience to the divine commandments
living he shall live and shall not die

choices.why: Scripture's phrase for the obedience of believers, kept distinct from perfect fulfilment of the law.

sections.title: Christ in Revelation blesses those who keep the commandments
sections.pass_a: VIII. To the same end also tends what Christ in the Apocalypse at last pronounces blessed those who keep the commandments of God. But all those who indulge vices, & who love & make a lie, he declares are to be shut out from the city of God. Blessed, he says, are they who keep his commandments, that their power may be in the tree of life, & they may enter by the gates into the city. But outside are dogs, & sorcerers, & the unchaste, & murderers, & servers of idols, & everyone who loves & makes a lie, Apoc. 22.
pass_b: Thesis VIII. The same point is made when Christ in the Book of Revelation calls blessed, in the end, those who keep God's commandments, and declares that all who give themselves to vice and who love and practise falsehood are to be shut out of God's city.

'Blessed', he says, 'are those who keep his commandments, so that they may have the right to the tree of life and enter the city through its gates. Outside are the dogs, the sorcerers, the impure, the murderers, the idolaters, and everyone who loves and practises falsehood' (Rev. 22).

lemmas.gloss: to be shut out from the city of God

choices.why: Scripture's phrase for the obedience of believers, kept distinct from perfect fulfilment of the law.

sections.title: No one belongs to Christ who does not keep the commandments
sections.pass_a: IX. Nor indeed is anyone in communion with Christ, or can he be judged truly to know & love him, who does not keep the commandments of God. In this we know, says John, that we have known him, if we observe his commandments. He who says he knows God, & does not keep his commandments, is a liar, & the truth is not in him. 1 John 2. & chap. 3. He who keeps his commandments abides in him, & he in him. Likewise chap. 5. This is the charity of God that we keep his commandments. Whence it is that Paul, 1 Cor. 7. teaches that only the observance of the commandments of God is of any moment in Christ, Circumcision, he says, is nothing: & uncircumcision is nothing: but the observance of the commandments of God.
pass_b: Thesis IX. No one who fails to keep God's commandments is in communion with Christ or can be thought truly to know and love him. John says: 'By this we know that we have known him, if we keep his commandments. Whoever says he knows God but does not keep his commandments is a liar, and the truth is not in him' (1 John 2).

In chapter 3: 'Whoever keeps his commandments remains in him, and he in him'; and in chapter 5: 'This is the love of God, that we keep his commandments.' That is why Paul (1 Cor. 7) teaches that in Christ nothing counts for anything but keeping God's commandments: 'Circumcision is nothing and uncircumcision is nothing; what counts is keeping the commandments of God.'

lemmas.gloss: the observance of the commandments of God

choices.why: Scripture's phrase for the obedience of believers, kept distinct from perfect fulfilment of the law.

sections.title: The saints of Scripture kept God's commandments
sections.pass_a: X. But that the faithful through divine grace can keep the commandments of God experience itself proves most evidently of all. For, Scripture being witness, many holy & godly men have in fact kept the commandments of God. David does not fear to affirm this of himself, Psal. 119. [margin: Pausa Heth] I hastened, he says, & did not delay to keep your commandments. Again, [margin: Pausa Schin] My soul has kept your testimonies: & has loved them exceedingly. I have kept your commandments & your testimonies: because all my ways are in your sight. And Luke the Evangelist bears the same witness of Zacharias & Elizabeth his wife. They were, he says, both righteous before God, walking in all the commandments & ordinances of the Lord, without complaint. Indeed all the godly & faithful are frequently described in scripture as those who keep the commandments of God: As when David says in the psalm just cited, I am a companion of all who fear you, & who keep your commandments.
pass_b: Thesis X. Experience itself proves most clearly of all that the faithful can keep God's commandments through God's grace, since Scripture testifies that many holy and devout people actually kept them. David does not hesitate to say so of himself in Psalm 119: 'I made haste and did not delay to keep your commandments' (margin: Pausa Heth); and again, 'My soul has kept your testimonies and loved them dearly. I have kept your commandments and your testimonies, for all my ways are before you' (margin: Pausa Schin).

Luke the Evangelist gives the same testimony of Zechariah and his wife Elizabeth: 'Both were righteous before God, walking blamelessly in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord.' Indeed, Scripture often describes all the devout and faithful as those who keep God's commandments, as when David says in the same psalm, 'I am a companion of all who fear you and keep your commandments.'

lemmas.gloss: have in fact kept the commandments of God

choices.why: Scripture's phrase for the obedience of believers, kept distinct from perfect fulfilment of the law.

sections.title: God's commandments are not burdensome
sections.pass_a: XI. And so rightly does John in the first epistle chap. five affirm that the commandments of God are not heavy. For, besides the fact that they demand nothing from us which is not very agreeable to nature & reason, & most advantageous to us, God also supplies strength to his own, through which they can carry out his commandments, & through his grace brings it about, that the godly & faithful observe them.
pass_b: Thesis XI. John is therefore right to say, in the fifth chapter of his first epistle, that God's commandments are not burdensome. They require nothing of us that is not in close accord with nature and reason and very much to our good.
Besides this, God gives his own people the strength to carry out his commandments, and by his grace he ensures that the devout and faithful keep them.

lemmas.gloss: that the commandments of God are not heavy

choices.why: Scripture's phrase for the obedience of believers, kept distinct from perfect fulfilment of the law.

sections.title: In some sense the regenerate fulfil the law
sections.pass_a: XII. Further, since the faithful, in whom divine grace works, are said in scripture to keep the commandments of God, there is no doubt that in some sense also they can be said to fulfil the law of God. For the commandments of God are the same as the law of God. And to keep the commandments of God, & to fulfil the same, signify one & the same thing. And certainly it cannot be denied that true & sincere charity, that is, love of God & of the neighbour, is found in those who are regenerated by the spirit of God. For those who believe in Christ, & are born again by his spirit, have passed from death to life. But, as John the Apostle testifies, He who does not love abides in death. 1 John 3. And accordingly whoever live by the spiritual life, necessarily love God & their neighbour. But charity is the fulfilling of the law, & he who loves, has fulfilled the law, as Paul expressly teaches, Rom. 13.
pass_b: Thesis XII. Since Scripture says that the faithful, in whom God's grace is at work, keep God's commandments, they can no doubt also be said in some sense to fulfil God's law. God's commandments are the same thing as his law, and to keep God's commandments and to fulfil them mean one and the same.

Nor can it be denied that true and sincere charity, the love of God and of one's neighbour, is found in those reborn by God's Spirit. Those who believe in Christ and have been born again by his Spirit have passed from death to life, and, as the apostle John testifies, 'whoever does not love remains in death' (1 John 3).
So all who live the spiritual life necessarily love God and their neighbour. Love is the fulfilment of the law, and whoever loves has fulfilled the law, as Paul expressly teaches in Romans 13.

lemmas.gloss: love of God and of the neighbour
charity is the fulfilling of the law

choices.why: The locus question: whether and how far a person can fulfil the law through Christ's grace.

sections.title: The righteousness of the law fulfilled in us
sections.pass_a: XIII. Moreover that the righteousness of the law is fulfilled in us, & that we fulfil the law & its righteousness seem to come to plainly the same thing. Now the Apostle teaches that Christ came into this world so that the righteousness of the law might be fulfilled in us, who walk not according to the flesh, but according to the spirit. For, he says, what was impossible for the law, because it was weak through the flesh, God sending his son, in the likeness of sinful flesh, & concerning sin, condemned sin in the flesh, so that the justification, or righteousness of the law might be fulfilled in us, who walk not according to the flesh, but according to the spirit. Rom. 8.
pass_b: Thesis XIII. Again, 'the righteousness of the law is fulfilled in us' and 'we fulfil the law and its righteousness' seem to say exactly the same thing. Now the apostle teaches that Christ came into this world so that the law's righteousness would be fulfilled in us, who live by the Spirit and not by the flesh.

'What the law could not do,' he says in Romans 8, 'because the flesh made it weak, God did by sending his own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh, and for sin: he condemned sin in the flesh, so that the justification, or righteousness, of the law would be fulfilled in us, whose walk follows the Spirit and not the flesh.'

come to plainly the same thing
what was impossible for the law

sections.title: But the regenerate cannot fulfil the law perfectly
sections.pass_a: XIV. Further, although those who are led by the spirit of God can be said in a true & fitting sense to fulfil the law of God, & to keep his commandments, according to the style & usage of Scripture: yet they are far from being able to fulfil the law perfectly, & to render to the precepts of God an exact obedience, complete in all its parts.
pass_b: Thesis XIV. In Scripture's way of speaking, then, those led by God's Spirit may truly and fittingly be said to fulfil God's law and keep his commandments.
Still, they are far from able to fulfil the law perfectly, or to give God's precepts an exact obedience that is complete in every part.

lemmas.gloss: in a true and fitting sense
according to the style and usage of Scripture

choices.why: Le Blanc's strict sense: satisfying the law in every respect, according to its full rigour.

sections.title: What it is to fulfil the law perfectly
sections.pass_a: XV. For to fulfil the law perfectly is to satisfy the law in every respect, according to its whole rigour, & not to fail in any of those things, which the law taken strictly demands of a man, so that he can by force of the legal covenant, according to the Clause Do & live, come to life, & claim by his own right the happiness which the law promises, without any fear of the punishments which the law threatens to transgressors. But no one fulfils the law in that sense & respect, except he who is wholly free from sin, & has never transgressed the law. For all who have sinned even once, the law taken strictly judges & condemns, & consigns to the curse, according to that other terrible Clause, Cursed is everyone who has not continued in all things which are written in the book of this law to do them. Indeed the law justifies & absolves no one freely, but only as of debt, according to Paul's doctrine, Rom. 4. But every sinner, whoever he may be, needs the grace & mercy of God, & cannot be justified except freely.
pass_b: Thesis XV. To fulfil the law perfectly is to satisfy it in every respect and in all its rigour, falling short in nothing that the law, strictly taken, requires of a person. Such a person could then reach life by virtue of the legal covenant, under its clause 'Do this and you will live', and claim as his right the happiness the law promises, with no fear of the penalties it threatens against those who break it.

No one fulfils the law in that sense and in that respect except someone entirely free of sin who has never broken it. All who have sinned even once are judged, condemned and handed over to the curse by the law strictly taken, under its other, terrible clause: 'Cursed is everyone who does not continue in all the things written in the book of this law, to do them.'
The law justifies and acquits no one freely, but only as a matter of debt, as Paul teaches in Romans 4. Every sinner, whoever he is, needs God's grace and mercy and can be justified only freely.

lemmas.gloss: by force of the legal covenant

choices.english: Do this and you will live
choices.why: The 'clause' of the legal covenant, set against its curse.

sections.title: No one has never broken the law
sections.pass_a: XVI. Now there is no one among men who has not at some time transgressed the law. Since all are born in sin, & are by nature slaves of sin, indeed dead in sins, and would lie perpetually in that death & slavery, unless they were raised & freed from it through the grace of Christ. Which we have briefly shown above: & Scripture inculcates the same so often & so plainly, that it would seem superfluous to gather its testimonies on this matter. Especially Paul presses & urges this doctrine quite often in his Epistles, & most of all in the one which he wrote to the Romans in the first four chapters. Where by many arguments he proves, That all have sinned & That all, both Jews and Greeks, are under sin, according to those sayings of Scripture, There is none righteous, there is none who understands, there is none who seeks God. All have turned aside, together they have become unprofitable; there is none who does good, there is not even to one. Whence he concludes that no one is justified before God by the works of the law: but that all are justified freely by the grace of God through the redemption which is in Christ Jesus. And from this it follows that there is no one who fulfils the law of God perfectly & in every respect: since, if anyone fulfilled the law in that way, without doubt he would be justified by the works of the law, and that of debt, not of grace.
pass_b: Thesis XVI. Yet there is no human being who has not broken the law at some time. All are born in sin; by nature they are slaves of sin, indeed dead in sins, and would lie for ever in that death and slavery unless Christ's grace raised and freed them. We showed this briefly above, and Scripture drives it home so often and so plainly that collecting its testimonies on the point would seem superfluous.

Paul above all presses the doctrine in his epistles, especially in the first four chapters of Romans. There he proves by many arguments that all have sinned and that all, Jews and Greeks alike, are under sin, in line with the scriptural sayings: 'No one is righteous, no one understands, no one seeks God. All have turned away; together they have become worthless. No one does good, not even one.'

From this he concludes that no one is justified before God by works of the law, but that all are justified freely by God's grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus. It follows that no one fulfils God's law perfectly and in every respect. If anyone did, he would surely be justified by works of the law, and that as a matter of debt, not of grace.

lemmas.latin: ex debito, non autem ex gratia

choices.why: Le Blanc's strict sense: satisfying the law in every respect, according to its full rigour.

sections.title: Even the holiest sin daily
sections.pass_a: XVII. But not only are men by nature sunk in sin, & convicted of sin by the law: but even after they are reborn through grace, they are far from rendering to the law an obedience perfect in every way. For all the holiest fall daily into many sins: According to that saying of James, In many things we all offend. [margin: Jas. 3] And John's first epistle chap. 1. If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, & the truth is not in us. With which agrees what the wise man pronounces, Eccl. chap. 7. There is not a righteous man on earth who does good, & does not sin.
pass_b: Thesis XVII. Not only are people sunk in sin by nature and convicted of sin by the law; even after they are reborn by grace, they are far from giving the law a perfect obedience in every respect. Even the holiest fall into many sins every day.

So James says, 'We all stumble in many things' (margin: Jas. 3), and John in chapter 1 of his first epistle, 'If we say we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us.' The wise man agrees in Ecclesiastes 7: 'There is no righteous man on earth who does good and never sins.'

lemmas.gloss: an obedience perfect in every way
In many things we all offend

choices.why: Le Blanc's strict sense: satisfying the law in every respect, according to its full rigour.

sections.title: The regenerate also fall into grave sins
sections.pass_a: XVIII. Nor do men regenerated through the grace of Christ remain liable only to lighter & small sins: but there are hardly any of them who do not sometimes fall into grave sins; by which they are held bound by a new guilt of eternal death, & lose their present fitness for the heavenly kingdom, until, God's special grace stirring them, they rise again from there through a particular repentance. The frequent falls of the saints recorded in Scripture make this manifest, as of David, who fell into adultery & murder: & of Peter, who three times denied Christ with an oath. And the daily experience of the faithful confirms the same all too often.
pass_b: Thesis XVIII. Those reborn by Christ's grace remain liable not only to lighter and smaller sins; hardly any of them fail at some time to fall into grave sins. Through these they are held bound by a fresh guilt of eternal death and lose their present fitness for the kingdom of heaven, until God's special grace stirs them and they rise again by a particular repentance.

The frequent falls of the saints recorded in Scripture show this, such as David's, who fell into adultery and murder, and Peter's, who denied Christ three times with an oath. The daily experience of the faithful confirms it all too often.

present fitness for the heavenly kingdom
